verification.note: Tables 3 to 10 parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber table extraction, specimen columns assigned from the header cells) and compared cell by cell with page images rendered at 2.6x; number resistant over number tested was also recomputed for every cell and all differences over 1 point are noted on the cell. Chart values (Figures 9, 11, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22) are printed data labels from the text layer: each label was assigned to the bar whose end it sits next to on the same row, the series from the legend swatch colours, and the bar length measured against the axis ticks agreed with the label within 0.1 point for every bar; 0% labels of zero-length bars were placed by row position; every chart was also checked by eye on the rendered page. Page numbers are PDF page numbers, which equal the printed page numbers in this report.

sources.notes: First annual report of AARSNET, the Assam state AMR surveillance network under NCDC (nodal centre Gauhati Medical College and Hospital, 12 government medical colleges): 14,179 priority-pathogen isolates from 13,369 unique patients in 2025 (the Discussion gives different totals: 14,346 reported, 11,834 and 13,299 after deduplication). Values are % resistant as printed. Genus-level organisms as printed. Pus aspirate (aspirated purulent material from a closed infected site; pus and wound swabs excluded) is mapped to deep; other sterile body fluids (CSF, pleural, peritoneal, synovial, pericardial) to sterile; IPD to ward. Location rows pool all specimens and carry no n (not printed with the charts); Table 4 location counts are recorded as counts. Several location figures do not reconcile with the specimen tables (S. aureus linezolid, Pseudomonas gentamicin, E. coli co-trimoxazole), see cell notes. Table 4 location counts do not sum to the Table 3 totals for Klebsiella (2,861 against 2,890), Pseudomonas (1,121 against 1,065) and S. aureus (1,684 against 1,711).
issues: Lead 2026-09-26: four figures the report contradicts (Enterococcus urine ciprofloxacin, E. coli urine co-trimoxazole, Pseudomonas gentamicin in the OPD and IPD chart) are marked as conflicts: shown with a caution, never pooled or used by reasoning.

Second reader 2026-09-26: the seeded sample of 117 of 469 cells (every table and chart) and all 21 table row n re-read on page images (scale 2.6 to 3.5) and compared with the file: 0 errors. Beyond the sample, all 233 table cells (Tables 5 to 10, value and number tested, resistant count recomputed) were compared with an independent parse of the text layer (specimen columns assigned from the header cells, since their order differs between tables), all 236 chart values (Figure 9 OSBF series, Figures 11, 14, 16, 18, 20 and 22) were re-assigned to bars independently (series from the legend swatch colour, every label within 0.6 point of its bar length, 0% labels of zero-length bars placed by slot position and checked by eye), and all 46 counts (Tables 3 and 4) were re-read: 0 discrepancies, nothing corrected.

Cells not kept by the validator, all printed that way: Enterococcus blood nitrofurantoin 40%R (42 of 104); Enterococcus urine ciprofloxacin 49%R with 730 resistant of 361 tested (no nt recorded, on purpose); E. coli urine co-trimoxazole 0%R (1 of 2,979); E. coli pus fosfomycin 3%R (5 of 169) and nitrofurantoin 31%R (10 of 32); E. coli blood fosfomycin 1%R (1 of 88); Figure 20 Pseudomonas gentamicin OPD 0% (zero-length bar in the OPD slot) and IPD 1%. The validator reports no count-table mismatch.

For the lead (not changed): E. coli pus cefuroxime is printed 86%R but its printed counts give 224 of 273 = 82%; by the brief that is a conflict, the file has it as a cell note only. Klebsiella blood colistin printed 0.009%R (2 of 207 = 1.0%) is likewise a note only.
Lead 2026-09-26: E. coli pus aspirate cefuroxime (printed 86% resistant, its counts give 224 of 273 = 82%) recorded as a conflict, as the conflict rule requires for gaps of a point or more.

sources.notes: Das PP et al., J Pure Appl Microbiol 2023;17(3):1591-1604. Assam Medical College & Hospital, Dibrugarh (institution-wide, AMRSN/ICMR site). Study period Oct 2018-Mar 2021. All susceptibility data reported as %RESISTANT (R%) in Table 2 (Gram-negatives) and Table 3 (Gram-positives); every cell converted to %S = 100 - R with from_R:true. Table 2 organisms labelled Klebsiella spp./Proteus spp./Enterobacter spp. mapped to K. pneumoniae/P. mirabilis/E. cloacae with per-cell notes (Klebsiella predominantly K. pneumoniae per abstract). Citrobacter kept as genus. n values taken from Table 2 headers (Acinetobacter n=687, Pseudomonas n=646); note text on p.9 gives slightly different NFGNB counts (A. baumannii n=550, P. aeruginosa n=590). Cefepime, Tobramycin (except Pseudomonas), Minocycline (except Acinetobacter) etc. were ND (not done) for several organisms and omitted. Colistin: MIC-tested on only 261 pooled GN isolates, all susceptible (not organism-specific, so not added per organism). S. aureus vancomycin s=100 added because text states VRSA not detected. MRSA 44.7% = cefoxitin resistance. VRE overall 1

sources.notes: Source: Panigrahi et al., Cureus 2025;17(10):e94006 (KIMS Bhubaneswar). Data taken from Table 2 (page 10), which prints Sensitive/Intermediate/Resistant counts and percentages for each of 13 drugs across the whole study population and 4 subgroups (ICU, non-ICU, CAI, HAI). I extracted the overall Total (n=7,942) Sensitive % values as printed (%S only; Intermediate not added). Values match the abstract/text (tigecycline 74.79%S, gentamicin 39.45%S, meropenem 34.34%S, piptazo 32.44%S). Note the scope hint 'cipro 78.4%R' corresponds to the Resistant column (6,227, 78.40%R); the reported %S for ciprofloxacin is 19.08% (I:2.50%), so no %R conversion was needed as %S is printed directly. CPS = cefoperazone-sulbactam mapped to non-canonical token 'cefoperazonesulbactam' (distinct from plain cefoperazone). Only organism studied is K. pneumoniae; other Klebsiella species excluded by authors. Subgroup rows (ICU/non-ICU/CAI/HAI) also available in Table 2 but only the overall pooled figures extracted here. VITEK 2, CLSI 2022 breakpoints.
issues: Lead 2026-09-26: its own institution key (KIMS_BHUBANESWAR_KLEB, was KIMS_BHUBANESWAR): a different study from the same hospital is not an earlier edition of this one.

sources.notes: Source: Poddar et al., Cureus 18(3):e104772 (2026), KIMS Bhubaneswar, Odisha; retrospective sterile-body-fluid antibiogram, Jan 2021-Dec 2022. 2307 samples, 291 isolates (12.6% positive); GPC 54%, S. aureus most common (92/291), MRSA 48.9%; K. pneumoniae top GNB (40), E. coli (27), Acinetobacter (24), Pseudomonas (19). All susceptibility data are presented ONLY as unlabeled bar charts (Fig 1 = Gram-positive: S. aureus, CONS, Enterococcus; Fig 2 = Gram-negative: K. pneumoniae, E. coli, Pseudomonas spp., Acinetobacter spp.) plus narrative sentences. There are NO numeric susceptibility tables. Color->drug map validated by matching extracted values to the paper's own text (Acinetobacter imipenem 41.9 vs 'imipenem 41%', gentamicin 41.5 vs 'aminoglycosides 41%', cotrimoxazole 36.8 vs '37.5%', ciprofloxacin 36.8 vs '38%'; E. coli ciprofloxacin 10.8 vs 'ciprofloxacin resistance high 90%'; Pseudomonas ceftazidime 20.9 vs '21%', ciprofloxacin 9.9 vs '10-11%'). Values are %
issues: Staph aureus text-derived cells (linezolid 95.65, dapto 95, TGC 92, VA/TEI 90.21): the paper states these for 'Staphylococcus spp.' collectively (Fig 1 has separate S. aureus and CoNS bar groups). Assigning them specifically to S. aureus is a reasonable but not certain mapping; the 95.65% 'highest' value could belong to either Staph group.

Pseudomonas amikacin s=20.9 is read as LOWER than meropenem/cefepime (25.9), but the text explicitly says Pseudomonas showed 'highest sensitivity to amikacin, followed by carbapenems', i.e., amikacin should exceed the carbapenems. Bar-read ordering is inconsistent with the text; value is approximate so not force-corrected, but flag for review.

Klebsiella ampicillin s=41.9 (bar read) is clinically implausible since K. pneumoniae is intrinsically ampicillin-resistant (expected ~0%); cannot confirm from the rendered bar chart. Possible misread of the AMP bar.
Oxacillin s=51.1 is a valid 100-R conversion from MRSA 48.9% (45/92); direction correct.

All remaining Gram-negative per-drug numbers are pixel reads off Figure 2 bar chart and cannot be independently confirmed to the stated decimal precision; they are appropriately flagged approx and are broadly consistent with the text ranges (amikacin 41-63%, carbapenems 40-60%, E. coli cipro ~10%).
Lead 2026-09-26: its own institution key (KIMS_BHUBANESWAR_STERILE, was KIMS_BHUBANESWAR): a different study from the same hospital is not an earlier edition of this one.

verification.note: Part 1: Part A of the report (chapters 1 to 3). Every table was parsed from the text layer with pdfplumber, every cell was checked arithmetically (printed n/N against the printed %), and every value was then compared by eye against page renders at scale 2.2 to 2.4 (wide tables cut into halves or thirds). Source inconsistencies found this way are recorded as printed with notes (M. morganii urine amikacin, A. baumannii ward colistin, S. maltophilia ceftazidime and others). Part 2: Part B (chapters 4 to 9). Every extracted table was parsed from the PDF text layer by script (pdfplumber tables and text lines, no retyping) and then compared value by value by eye against page images rendered at scale 2.2 to 3.2 and cropped by column group: Tables 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 5.1 to 5.9, 6.1, 6.2, 6.4 to 6.15, 6.17, 7.1 to 7.4, 8.3, 9.27 to 9.29 and 9.39 to 9.41 (Table 9.44, also compared, is excluded: see excluded). Every printed n/N was also checked arithmetically against its printed percentage; the source inconsistencies found are recorded as printed with a row or per-drug note.

sources.notes: ICMR AMRSN 2024, part A: Enterobacterales (chapter 2) and non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli (chapter 3), plus isolation counts from chapter 1. 99,027 culture-positive isolates from the network's tertiary-care centres. Enterobacterales rows are 'all specimens except urine and faeces' (spec nonurine) by location, urine rows are all locations; non-fermenter rows are 'all samples (except faeces)' (spec all) by location and by specimen. Colistin figures are percent intermediate. CR and CS rows are carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets. Counts: Table 1.3 by location (all specimens) and Tables 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 by specimen (all locations); the two sets overlap, so their sum is not an isolate total. CoNS counts are the Table 1.13 CoNS total; Enterococcus spp. counts are the unspeciated group of Table 1.17 (E. faecalis and E. faecium are counted separately). Part B of the ICMR AMRSN 2024 annual report (merged by the lead with Part A, chapters 1 to 3): typhoidal Salmonella, diarrhoeal pathogens, staphylococci and enterococci, fungi, S. pneumoniae (invasive, Table 8.3) and ICU HAI surveillance susceptibility (cohort "hai"). Cells printed as "(-)" (too few isolates) are left out. Fungal tables print S, I/SDD and R; only S is recorded. Several fungal percentages are printed 0.1 above the count ratio (e.g. 17/18 printed 94.5); recorded as printed. Isolates come from tertiary care hospitals; the report says the data do not reflect community AMR (p5). The ICMR network report for 2024 (21 regional centres; 99,027 culture-positive isolates). Extracted in two parts by table chapter and merged; the transcribed national summary used before this is superseded.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell of every extracted table was re-read by eye from page renders (scale 2.5 to 4, cropped by column group) before comparing with the file: all 1,321 cells (the seeded 25% sample of 330 cells from sample_cells.py plus all the rest), all 158 row n, every printed tested count (nt), all 163 isolation counts (Tables 1.3, 1.5, 1.10, 1.13, 1.17) and all 22 trend series year by year (1,290 points, Tables 2.6, 2.7, 2.9, 2.17, 2.18, 3.3, 3.6, 3.9, 3.12, 4.3, 4.4, 5.2, 5.4, 5.5, 5.7, 5.9, 6.4, 6.8, 6.9, 6.11, 6.15, 6.17).

Second reader: 0 transcription errors found: no wrong value, n, nt, count or trend year, no OPD/ward/ICU column swap, and specimen and setting mapping match each table heading; no table needed a correction re-read.

Second reader: the 6 conflict entries were checked on the page and are correct as written (M. morganii urine amikacin 121/154 (8.6); A. baumannii ward colistin 1927/1997 (69.5); S. maltophilia ceftazidime 21/36 (58.3) in Tables 3.7 and 3.9 vs 2/36 (5.6) in Table 3.8; P. aeruginosa BSI netilmicin 25/57 (38.6); Enterococcus spp. UTI vancomycin 18/98 (81.6); S. aureus UTI clindamycin 6/10 (16.0)).

Second reader: the 14 cells the validator does not keep (7 caution, 5 intrinsic, 2 hidden) are all printed that way, none is a transcription error. The E. faecium count mismatches (OPD 569 vs 570, ward 1791 vs 1793) are printed in Tables 6.14 and 1.3 (source inconsistency, already noted on the rows).

Second reader: the dropped trend point (K. pneumoniae urine cefazolin 2021, printed 1970/3560 (55.3), identical to amikacin 2021 on p87) is confirmed; the row note still said 'recorded as printed' and now says it was left out. Added a per-drug note for Table 6.14 E. faecalis ICU vancomycin, printed 287/312 (92) with ICU N=303 (source inconsistency; value unchanged).

CoNS species rows added 2026-09-26 (antibiogram-rules.js now has species keys): Table 6.10 (p155, 'CoNS isolated from all specimens', no location split; spec all, set all, like its S. saprophyticus row) columns S. haemolyticus (N=1572), S. epidermidis (N=1269) and S. hominis (N=1241), 9 cells each (27 in all) with n/N as printed. First reading from the text layer (pdfplumber words assigned to columns by the table's vertical grid lines), second from the page image (scale 3.2, cropped to the first three species columns, top and bottom halves); the two agreed on all 27 percentages, 27 n/N and 3 N. Every n/N was checked against its printed percentage: all agree except S. epidermidis tetracycline 250/460 printed 54.4 (54.348%, source rounding; per-drug note, recorded as printed). The excluded entry for these columns was removed.

Enterobacterales species rows added 2026-09-26 (antibiogram-rules.js now has keys koxytoca, kaerogenes, enterobacter and prettgeri): Table 2.1 (p56, nonurine/all) columns K. oxytoca (N=352, 10 cells), K. (Enterobacter) aerogenes (N=62, 8), Enterobacter spp. (N=229, 10) and P. rettgeri (N=88, 7); Table 2.14 (p79, urine/all) columns K. oxytoca (N=211, 13), Enterobacter spp. (N=87, 4) and P. rettgeri (N=33, 3); n/N as printed, cells printed (-) or - left out. Also the Table 2.8 yearly trend (p66, Enterobacter species, 2017 to 2024, 9 drugs, 72 points) on the nonurine Enterobacter spp. row, and the Table 1.5 Enterobacter spp. counts (p20, 8 specimens; urine 87 = the Table 2.14 N, total 316 = 229 + 87). No other susceptibility table of the report has these organisms (text search of all 206 pages, spacing ignored; chapter 9 lists them only in organism distributions). First reading from the text layer (pdfplumber words placed in cells by each table's ruling lines; the same parse reproduced all 177 cells already recorded from the other columns of Tables 2.1 and 2.14), second from page images (scale 4, target columns cropped beside the drug column); the two agreed on all 174 table items (15 N, 159 cells or trend points) and the 8 counts. Printed n/N against printed %: K. oxytoca urine ciprofloxacin 73/211 printed 34.4 (34.6%; re-read at scale 8, per-drug note) and three truncated Table 2.8 points (row note), all recorded as printed. Klebsiella spp. stays excluded (K. pneumoniae key); the excluded entries for Tables 2.1, 2.14 and 2.8 and for the Table 1.5 count rows were updated.

verification.note: Part 1: Part A of the report (chapter 1 organism counts, chapter 2 specimen-wise antibiograms of Enterobacterales and non-fermenters, chapters 3 and 4). Every susceptibility table was parsed from the PDF text layer with pdfplumber (no retyping), every cell was checked arithmetically (printed n/N against the printed %), and every value was then compared by eye against page renders at scale 2.2 to 2.6 (wide tables cut into two or three crops): Tables 2.7 to 2.9, 2.11 to 2.13, 2.16, 2.18 to 2.20, 3.1 to 3.5, 3.14, 3.19, 3.20, 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7, 4.8, 4.10 and 4.11. Count Tables 1.3, 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 were parsed from the text layer and compared by eye; Tables 2.2 to 2.4 were read from the page images and checked against the chapter 1 specimen totals. Source inconsistencies are recorded as printed with conflict entries or notes (colistin in Tables 2.11 to 2.13 and 2.16, the repeated colistin cell of Table 3.1, S. maltophilia OPD levofloxacin, denominators above the column n in Tables 3.19 and 3.20, sample-wise n in Tables 4.2 and 4.5). Part 2: Part B (chapter 2 tables for Part B organisms, chapters 5 to 10). Every table was parsed from the PDF text layer by script (pdfplumber tables, word boxes for Table 7.2, no retyping) and then compared value by value by eye against page renders at scale 2.2 to 3.0, cropped by table or half-table: Tables 2.10, 2.14, 2.15, 2.17, 2.21, 2.22, 5.1, 6.1, 6.3, 6.8, 7.1, 7.2, 7.5 to 7.7, 7.10, 7.12 to 7.14, 8.1 to 8.4, 9.2 to 9.4, 10.27 to 10.29, 10.39 and 10.40. Every printed n/N was checked arithmetically against its printed percentage; the OPD, ward and ICU counts of Tables 7.2 and 7.14 add up exactly to their Total columns, and Tables 2.14 and 2.15 add up to Table 7.13. The 2023 columns of the trend tables were compared with the tables used. Contradictions of 1 percentage point or more are recorded as conflict entries; smaller ones as notes.

sources.notes: ICMR AMRSN 2023, part A: organism counts (chapter 1 and chapter 2 section A), specimen-wise antibiograms by location for E. coli, K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii and P. aeruginosa (chapter 2 section B), Enterobacterales (chapter 3) and non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli (chapter 4). 99,492 culture-positive isolates from the network's tertiary-care centres. Enterobacterales rows are 'all specimens except urine and faeces' (spec nonurine) by location, urine rows are all locations; non-fermenter rows are 'all samples (except faeces)' (spec all) by location and by specimen. Chapter 2 rows give blood, urine and pus/exudates by location (no all-location column); pus/exudates is one specimen type within the report's superficial infections, so these pus rows and counts are narrower than the chapter 4 pus (superficial infection) rows. Colistin figures are percent intermediate (chapters 3 and 4 footnotes; chapter 2 prints no footnote), and in chapter 2 several printed colistin percentages disagree with their own counts (recorded as printed, with conflicts). CR and CS rows are carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets. The sample-wise non-fermenter tables (4.2, 4.5) print an n per specimen that matches the numbers tested, well below the isolate counts of Table 1.10. Counts: Table 1.3 by location (all specimens), Tables 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 by specimen (all locations), and the top-5 lists of Tables 2.2 to 2.4 by specimen and location (blood, urine, pus/exudates); the sets overlap, so their sum is not an isolate total. CoNS counts are the Table 1.13 CoNS total; Enterococcus spp. counts are the unspeciated group of Table 1.17. ICMR AMRSN 2023, part B: typhoidal Salmonella (blood), diarrhoeal pathogens (stool), staphylococci and enterococci, fungi, S. pneumoniae (national reference laboratory isolates) and ICU HAI surveillance susceptibility (cohort "hai"), plus the chapter 2 location tables for these organisms (S. Typhi blood, enterococci urine, S. aureus pus/exudates, faecal Salmonella and Aeromonas). 99,492 culture-positive isolates in the network in 2023. Cells printed as "(-)" (too few isolates) or as counts without a percentage are left out. Several percentages are printed about 0.05 above the count ratio (e.g. 50/415 printed 12.1); recorded as printed. The yearly trend tables (2017 to 2023) are not recorded: the 2024 edition covers 2017 to 2024.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the seeded sample (sample_cells.py, 239 cells) plus a seeded top-up that takes the chapter 2 specimen-by-location Tables 2.7 to 2.9, 2.11 to 2.13, 2.16 and 2.18 to 2.20 to 40% of their cells (295 sampled cells in all) was read from page images (scale 2.6 to 4.5, cropped by column group) before the extracted values were looked at; every table was in fact read in full, so all 955 cells (printed percentage and number tested), all 100 row n with organism, specimen, location and phenotype, and all 198 counts were compared with the file. 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected, so no table needed a re-read under the 2% rule. The cells the validator lists (values seen in its output first) were re-read in zoomed crops.

Location columns: every chapter 2 table prints OPD, ward, ICU in that order, and its column n match the location counts of Tables 2.2 to 2.4 wherever those list the organism (all but A. baumannii blood OPD), except P. aeruginosa pus ICU (below). Table 4.7 prints Total, Ward, ICU, OPD and is mapped correctly (OPD n=163). No OPD/ward/ICU swap found anywhere.

Conflicts confirmed as printed: colistin in Table 2.11 (1945/1970 printed 99.7%, 967/978 printed 99.6%, 305/305 printed 99.6%), Table 2.12 (535/554 97.3%, 450/484 96.1%, 170/173 94.4%), Table 2.13 (195/198 95.4%, 237/246 95.8%, 97/102 97.3%) and Table 2.16 ICU (117/177 printed 100); Table 3.1 colistin 305/327 (93.3) printed identically in the E. cloacae, Enterobacter spp. and P. mirabilis columns (the chapter text on PDF page 76 gives 93.3% for E. cloacae, so keeping the cell on E. cloacae and flagging the other two columns is right); S. maltophilia OPD levofloxacin 76/85 printed (88.4). Every conflict text quotes the right counts.

Other cells the validator does not keep are printed as recorded: fosfomycin in blood (E. coli 30/31, 71/73, 30/30; K. pneumoniae 9/14, 44/63, 39/75); intrinsic E. cloacae urine cefazolin 3/30 (10.0), P. mirabilis urine nitrofurantoin 5/68 (7.4), M. morganii urine nitrofurantoin 4/32 (12.5) and P. mirabilis colistin (the repeated cell above); hidden E. coli CR and CS nitrofurantoin 22/39 (56.4) and 67/77 (87.0).

The 15 count-table mismatches are printed that way (source, not transcription): P. aeruginosa pus ICU 122 in Table 2.4 against n=121 in Table 2.20; E. coli urine 10043 in Tables 1.2 and 1.5 (and 6022 + 3411 + 610 in Table 2.3) against n=10042 in Table 3.14; A. baumannii 11947 in Tables 1.2 and 1.3 (1260 + 6086 + 4601) against 11948 in Tables 1.10 and 4.1; and the 12 specimen columns of Tables 4.2 and 4.5, whose printed n is the number tested (A. baumannii blood 1270, LRT 3519, SI 1080, DI 334, CSF 156, urine 228; P. aeruginosa 583, 2262, 1663, 399, 40, 707), against the Table 1.10 isolate counts. Each already has a row note. (build-antibiogram.mjs was updated while this check ran and now lists 14: it no longer flags the A. baumannii pair, whose 11947 is a sum of location counts.)

Also confirmed against the pages: the cells printed as (-) and left out, the Klebsiella spp. columns of Tables 3.1 and 3.14, the Total columns of Tables 3.2 to 3.5 and the all-specimen columns of Tables 4.8 and 4.11 (identical to Table 3.1 and to the Total columns of Tables 4.7 and 4.10), the denominator notes of Tables 3.19 and 3.20, Table 1.2 LRT 5575 against 5576 in Table 1.10, and the polymyxin B and ticarcillin-clavulanate cells listed in excluded. Two rounding-only differences are rightly left without a conflict (Table 2.18 ward colistin 284/287 printed 98.9; Table 4.4 total colistin 2923/3037 printed 96.3). Counts not recorded (S. haemolyticus, S. epidermidis, S. hominis, S. Typhi, Klebsiella spp.) are listed in excluded with reasons. verification.status left as double-checked.

Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell of every extracted table re-read by eye from page renders (scale 2.5 to 4, dense tables cropped by column group) and written down before comparing with the file: all 840 cells with their printed number tested (the seeded 25% sample of 210 cells from sample_cells.py is part of this), all 104 row n, and every cell printed as (-), -, NT or counts only (all correctly left out). As asked, the chapter 2 location tables (2.10, 2.14, 2.15, 2.17, 2.21, 2.22) and the HAI tables (10.27 to 10.29, 10.39, 10.40) were read in full; Table 10.41 is counts only (N=6, 'numbers too low') and rightly excluded.

Second reader: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected: no wrong value, n or number tested, no OPD/ward/ICU column swap, no organism, phenotype or cohort mix-up (every HAI row has cohort hai; the chapter 2 urine ICU enterococcal rows of Tables 2.14 and 2.15 stay separate from the HAI UTI rows of Table 10.40), and every row's table and page are right. No table needed a correction re-read.

Second reader: the 2 cautions are printed that way: Table 7.1 S. aureus oxacillin 1689/4072 (35.9), confirmed at zoom, while Tables 7.2 (Total) and 7.4 (2023) print 1737/4071 (42.7); Table 10.39 E. coli UTI colistin 86/95 (93.5). The 7 intrinsic cells are printed as recorded: C. krusei fluconazole 15/40 (37.5) in Table 8.1 and 6/19 (31.6) in Table 8.2; HAI BSI K. pneumoniae ampicillin 3/136 (1.5), A. baumannii amoxicillin-clavulanate 3/26 (11.5), ampicillin 2/32 (6.3) and ertapenem 2/26 (7.7); HAI UTI K. pneumoniae ampicillin 1/26 (3.9). The 1 hidden cell, HAI UTI E. coli tigecycline 23/25 (92.0) (hidden by the urine tigecycline rule), is printed as recorded. The file has no count tables, so there are no count mismatches.

Second reader: every printed percentage re-computed from its printed counts. Only 6 are 0.5 points or more off, all printed that way and all already recorded: the 2 conflicts above, and as notes HAI BSI K. pneumoniae ampicillin 1.5 (3/136 = 2.2), HAI BSI E. coli tetracycline 30.1 (13/42 = 31.0), Table 7.6 MRSA clindamycin 66.2 (1225/1833 = 66.8) and Table 9.4 levofloxacin 96 (87/90 = 96.7).

Second reader: S. pneumoniae split checked against Tables 9.2 and 9.3 (p210 to 211): the CSF row (n=11) is the meningeal-criteria column, penicillin 3/11 (27.27) and cefotaxime 9/11 (81.80); the blood row's penicillin 62/63 (98.41) and cefotaxime 63/63 (100) are the 63 non-meningeal isolates, and its other six agents and its n=74 are Table 9.3 (all invasive isolates). Values and numbers tested match the page. Two judgement calls, both stated in the row notes and left as they are: the page does not say the 11 meningeal isolates are CSF isolates (meningeal is the breakpoint set), and the 74 invasive isolates include those 11 and come from blood, CSF and sterile fluids (p207), so the blood row stands for all invasive isolates.

Second reader: stratum calls and note cross-references checked on the pages and correct: Table 6.3 is headed 'All Specimens' but its S. flexneri counts are exactly the OPD plus ward faecal counts of Table 2.23, so stool is right; 'Salmonella spp. Faecal' (Table 1.27: 307 isolates, OPD 96, ward 210, ICU 1) is the group Table 1.28 calls 'Non Typhoidal Salmonella' (307/773 in 2023); Table 5.4 prints S. Paratyphi A levofloxacin 4/19 as 21.1; Table 6.6 has only the V. cholerae column, all (-); Table 10.45 does repeat identical counts across many agents, as its exclusion says.

CoNS species rows added 2026-09-26 (antibiogram-rules.js now has species keys): Table 7.10 (p176, 'CoNS isolated from all specimens', no location split; spec all, set all, like its S. saprophyticus row) columns S. haemolyticus (n=2262), S. epidermidis (n=2056) and S. hominis (n=1408), 9 cells each (27 in all) with n/N as printed. First reading from the text layer (pdfplumber words assigned to cells by the table's grid lines), second from the page image (scale 3.4, first three species columns cropped in two halves); the two agreed on all 27 percentages, 27 n/N and 3 n, and every n/N gives its printed percentage. The excluded entry for these columns was removed.

verification.note: migrated from data/antibiogram-raw.json: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026)

sources.notes: Source: Gautam et al, Indian J Med Res 2019;149:208-215 (ICMR multi-centric ESBL study, 4 tertiary centres: AIIMS Delhi, PGIMER Chandigarh, CMC Vellore, JIPMER Puducherry; Oct 2014-Mar 2016). Study covers ONLY E. coli (341 isolates) and K. pneumoniae (304 isolates), no P. aeruginosa, A. baumannii, S. aureus, or Enterococcus. Method: Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion, CLSI. Table II reports % SUSCEPTIBLE by centre; Table III reports % RESISTANT (n/N) split by ESBL-producer vs non-ESBL. I derived OVERALL susceptibility by pooling Table III ESBL + non-ESBL resistant counts per drug (s = 100 - pooled %R, from_R:true for all pooled cells). Colistin values taken directly from the printed overall figures in the Results text (E. coli 99% = 271/274; K. pneumoniae 98% = 229/234), not from R. CAVEAT: Table III denominators (e.g. 167+202=369 for E. coli, 98+126=224 for K. pneumoniae) exceed stated collection totals of 341/304, likely reflecting drug-specific tested subsets/classification; per-drug pooled %R is nevertheless computed directly from printed n/N. Individual per-centre susceptibility values are available in Table II if centre-level breakdown is preferred. ESBL prevalence context: CDT dete
issues: Lead 2026-09-26: a multicentre research study, not a surveillance network report: kind "study", with a focus (two organisms, 2014 to 2016): shown, never pooled, not a profile.

verification.note: Tables 6 to 14 parsed from the PDF text layer (PyMuPDF words grouped into rows by position) and every value then compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 2.2 and cropped into halves. sources.notes: Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 18, No. 1 (published April 2012), data January to December 2011, 8 pages; the older edition of the layout used in 2024. Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus wound swab; body fluids; respiratory isolates): organism pie charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, legend counts and an "others" list) and GPC and GNB percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus, sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)" is recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci. Combined columns: "Imipenem / Meropenem" (every GNB table) is recorded under meropenem and "Vancomycin/Teicoplanin" under vancomycin, each cell noted; the "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded; blood Salmonella also print nalidixic acid separately (recorded). The pus and body fluid GNB tables print cefoperazone-sulbactam before piperacillin-tazobactam; every table was mapped by its own headers. Blood S. pneumoniae OPD penicillin is printed "90*" with the footnote "1 isolate was moderately sensitive". Colistin and tigecycline are printed as percent susceptible for Enterobacterales and non-fermenters; no interpretive criteria are stated for them beyond "CLSI 2010". Isolate numbers: pus coagulase-negative staphylococci OPD (chart 87, table 82) and ward (chart 45, table 44) disagree; both recorded as printed and noted on the rows. The respiratory ward chart prints "Others - 54", but its "others" list sums to 43, and the legend plus 43 equals the printed 352 isolates. Several percentages cannot be produced by the row's n (per-drug tested numbers are not printed; for example pus ICU coagulase-negative staphylococci n=8, penicillin 11); recorded as printed. Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Serratia marscecens", "Morgnella", "Elizebethkingia", "S. maltophila", "Strept. viridans" as viridans group streptococci); "Salmonella typhimurium" is recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella; entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Fungal isolates are counted in the charts; their susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. The live URL no longer exists; the PDF was retrieved from the Wayback Machine copy https://web.archive.org/web/20120512183945id_/http://sgrh.com/newsletters/mb%20apr%202012.pdf and opens completely (8 pages, 428 KB, not truncated).

sources.notes: Antibiogram section (printed pages 6 to 17, PDF pages 14 to 25) of the SKNMC and GH Antibiotic Policy for Hospital, Version 2.1, dated 15 December 2024 (implementation 1 January 2025). Only organism-level lists are recorded: the 11 'Pseudomonas (n=...)' lines, one per box, and the Respiratory-ICU Gram-positive list, which that box attributes entirely to Staphylococcus aureus (prevalence 100% of the Gram-positive cocci). The pooled Gram-positive and Gram-negative lists mix several organisms and are left out (see excluded), so this file does not give E. coli, Klebsiella, Acinetobacter or enterococcal figures even though the boxes name them. Syndromes are recorded as specimens: BSI as blood, UTI as urine, respiratory as respiratory, SSTI as pus. IPD is recorded as wards because each syndrome has a separate ICU box. There is no BSI-OPD box. The data period is printed only as 2024 without months; since the policy is dated 15 December 2024 it cannot include all of December 2024. The Pseudomonas n printed on each line does not match the Pseudomonas share given in the prevalence column (a percentage of the Gram-negative group), so it may count only tested or only P. aeruginosa isolates; recorded as printed. Pseudomonas lines print 'Pipracillin', recorded as piperacillin. Page numbers are PDF pages (printed page number plus 8).
